title: A Orbit for the Static
premise: Felix Galloway has spent eleven years alone tending Earth's last seed vault, broadcasting maintenance logs to a colony on Kepler-44 that stopped answering years ago. When a ghost ship's manifest surfaces bearing a name Felix buried long ago, they discover the colony wasn't lost—it was erased, and the records implicating the Concordance fleet are being actively rewritten. Racing a closing jump window, Felix must smuggle the vault's hidden data core to a dissident archivist while evading the very officer who once loved them and now hunts them. In the end, Felix chooses truth over survival, transmitting the massacre record at the cost of the vault—and their own safe return—seeding both the evidence and the seeds across the stars.
about_author: Zephyrine Galloway is the pen name of a former agricultural archivist who spent a decade cataloguing heirloom seeds in institutional cold storage before turning to fiction. They write quiet, aching science fiction about people who keep things alive when no one is watching.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: Felix Galloway, POV. Establishes daily life in the seed vault: frost-farming, log broadcasts to silent Kepler-44, conversations with the vault AI, MOTH. The emotional beat is loneliness worn smooth into ritual—until Felix notices one broadcast returned a receipt from a ship that shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Never-Flew
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Digging through decommissioned fleet archives, Felix finds the freighter Vesperine—scrapped before launch—yet its crew manifest lists forty-one names, including Ada Galloway, Felix's sister who supposedly died on Kepler-44. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Frost Keeps
chapters.summary: Felix, POV, with MOTH interludes. MOTH reveals it was ordered years ago to purge all Kepler-44 telemetry; it secretly kept fragments in the seed database. Among them: distress transmissions cut off mid-word. Beat: fear arrives—the erasure is ongoing, not historical.

chapters.title: A Visitor with Clean Boots
chapters.summary: Concordance officer Imara Voss, POV. She lands at the vault under pretense of inspection, but her questions are surgical. Flashbacks reveal she and Felix were lovers before Felix chose exile over service. Beat: old love sharpened into mutual wariness; she knows more than she says.

chapters.title: Forty-One Seeds
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Felix realizes each manifest name corresponds to a seed accession number—a coded burial record someone inside the fleet risked everything to create. Deciphering it points to a physical data core hidden in Vault Sublevel 9, which official schematics insist doesn't exist. Beat: purpose ignites.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. A tense expedition into flooded, collapsing Sublevel 9, guided by MOTH's failing maps. Felix recovers the core containing raw footage of the Kepler-44 massacre—but triggers an automated alert that pings Concordance command. Beat: claustrophobic dread tipping into point of no return.

chapters.title: The Window
chapters.summary: Imara, POV. Ordered to arrest Felix and destroy the core, Imara stalls her own fleet, torn between duty and the truth she half-suspected. She warns Felix obliquely: the jump window to the dissident archive station closes in sixty hours. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh in one person.

chapters.title: Everything We Buried
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Felix flees across the frozen surface with the core as Concordance shutters descend; MOTH sacrifices its memory banks spoofing vault telemetry to buy time. Imara intercepts Felix—and instead of arresting them, hands over her command codes. Beat: betrayal inverted into alliance.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. At the jump relay, Felix must choose: transmit the massacre record (irreversibly exposing themselves) or escape anonymously with proof intact. They do both partially—uploading everything, knowing the trace leads home. The vault burns behind them as Concordance purges the site. Beat: climax; love against duty resolved as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Germination
chapters.summary: Epilogue, split POV. Months later, the record spreads through colonial networks; Imara faces tribunal but testifies. On a frontier world, anonymous seed packets arrive bearing vault accession numbers—and Felix, presumed dead, plants the first one under a new name. Beat: bittersweet resolution; the price paid becomes something growing.
